The employment outlook will be Good for nurse aides, orderlies and patient service associates (NOC 33102) in Newfoundland and Labrador for the 2025-2027 period.

The following factors contributed to this outlook:

  • Employment growth will lead to a few new positions.
  • A moderate number of positions will become available due to retirements.
  • There are a moderate number of unemployed workers with recent experience in this occupation.

Demand for the services of this occupation is high and expected to increase, as the aging population requires more care. However, financial constraints are expected to somewhat dampen growth prospects. Facilities throughout the province have been reported as understaffed, resulting in large workloads and forced overtime. As such, there has been a lack of sufficient temporary staff needed to fill in for vacation, sick leave, and other absences by permanent employees. The provincial government has expanded its nursing college programs and has been using a variety of incentives such as cash bonuses to help address shortfalls.

The employment outlook will be Very good for nurse aides, orderlies and patient service associates (NOC 33102) in Prince Edward Island for the 2025-2027 period.

Prince Edward Island continues to face a high demand for workers in this occupation, driven by an aging population, growth in nursing and residential care facilities, and the need for 24-hour patient care. The Resident Care Worker Support Program remains active and has expanded, offering free tuition and financial assistance to candidates who commit to working in the province after graduation. In late 2025, the federal government also introduced a five-year tax credit for personal support workers, further improving the attractiveness of this career. Most workers are employed in nursing homes, hospitals, and community health centres, and flexible candidates willing to work long shifts are especially valued. For new graduates or career changers, this occupation offers stable employment, strong provincial and federal support, and clear pathways through immigration streams and training programs.

The aging population has resulted a major shortage of workers in this occupation. Increasing wages and tuition relief for training programs may serve to entice new entrants into the Continuing Care Assistant role. Further, some employers are offering incentives such as signing bonuses and in-house training paths to CCA certification. Jobseekers in this occupation should have little difficulty finding work regardless of which region of the province they live in, though owning a vehicle is a common requirement that may be a barrier to some applicants. The physically challenging nature of this job, which often involves shift work, has led to higher turnover than normal. Opportunities do occur in hospitals, but are more frequent in non-hospital settings.

Increased demand for health care services associated with an ageing population is expected to be among the primary drivers of employment growth in this occupation.   • These jobs usually involve shiftwork and are often physically demanding, mainly in the form of transporting, lifting and turning patients.
